questions.stem: Equilibrium price in a market is the price at which

options.text: quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
the producer earns the highest possible profit
the consumer pays the lowest possible amount
government has fixed the price by law

questions.explanation: Equilibrium simply means balance: buyers want exactly the quantity sellers are offering, so there is no unsatisfied buyer and no unsold stock to push the price either way.

distractorRationale.b: Maximum profit is the firm's objective, and it need not occur at the market-clearing price for the industry
distractorRationale.c: The lowest price consumers would like would leave a large shortage
distractorRationale.d: A legally fixed price is a controlled price, which is normally different from equilibrium

questions.stem: In a market for beans the schedule is: ₦100 — demand 80, supply 20; ₦200 — demand 60, supply 40; ₦300 — demand 50, supply 50; ₦400 — demand 40, supply 62. What is the equilibrium price in naira? Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Equilibrium occurs where the two quantities are equal. At ₦300 both demand and supply are 50 bags, so ₦300 clears the market and 50 bags is the equilibrium quantity.

questions.stem: Using the same beans schedule (₦200 — demand 60, supply 40), government fixes a maximum price of ₦200 per bag. The immediate result is

options.text: a surplus of 20 bags
a shortage of 20 bags
a shortage of 100 bags
no change in the market at all

questions.explanation: A maximum price below equilibrium keeps the price artificially low, so demand of 60 exceeds supply of 40 and 20 bags of demand go unsatisfied. That gap is what drives queues, hoarding and black market trading.

distractorRationale.a: Surpluses follow minimum prices set above equilibrium, not ceilings
distractorRationale.c: 100 is the sum of the two quantities rather than the difference between them
distractorRationale.d: A ceiling below equilibrium always bites; only a ceiling above equilibrium would be ineffective

questions.stem: If demand for cement increases while supply remains unchanged, the equilibrium

options.text: price rises and quantity rises
price rises and quantity falls
price falls and quantity rises
price falls and quantity falls

questions.explanation: A rightward shift of demand creates excess demand at the old price. As buyers bid the price up, producers extend supply along the unchanged supply curve, so the new equilibrium has both a higher price and a larger quantity traded.

distractorRationale.b: Quantity falls only when supply decreases, which has not happened here
distractorRationale.c: A falling price with a rising quantity is the result of an increase in supply
distractorRationale.d: Both falling is the result of a decrease in demand

questions.stem: A bumper harvest of tomatoes, with demand unchanged, will cause the equilibrium price to

options.text: rise, and the quantity traded to fall
fall, and the quantity traded to rise
rise, and the quantity traded to rise
remain the same, since demand has not changed

questions.explanation: A bumper harvest shifts supply to the right, creating excess supply at the old price. Sellers cut prices to clear the crop, and the lower price extends demand, so more tomatoes change hands at a lower price.

distractorRationale.a: That is the effect of a fall in supply, such as after flooding
distractorRationale.c: Price and quantity both rising indicates an increase in demand
distractorRationale.d: Equilibrium responds to a shift in either curve, not only to demand

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely consequence of a minimum price fixed above the equilibrium price?

options.text: A shortage that encourages black market trading
A surplus that government may have to buy into a buffer stock
An immediate fall in the cost of production
A rightward shift of the demand curve

questions.explanation: Holding the price above equilibrium encourages producers to supply more while discouraging buyers, so unsold output accumulates. Governments usually mop this up through buffer stock purchases or restrain it with production quotas.

distractorRationale.a: Shortages and black markets follow maximum prices set below equilibrium
distractorRationale.c: A price floor changes the price received, not the technology or input costs of production
distractorRationale.d: A higher enforced price contracts demand along the existing curve; it does not shift the curve

questions.stem: A maximum price fixed above the equilibrium price will have no effect on the market.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. A ceiling only binds if it prevents the price from rising to equilibrium. Set above equilibrium, the market simply settles at the lower equilibrium price and the law is never triggered.

distractorRationale.b: This assumes every legal limit bites; a ceiling higher than the market price is legally present but economically idle

questions.stem: In a market where the ruling price is above equilibrium, the process that restores equilibrium is best described as

options.text: unsold stock forcing sellers to cut price, which extends demand and contracts supply
disappointed buyers bidding the price up until supply expands
government stepping in to fix a new legal price
the demand curve shifting rightward until it meets supply

questions.explanation: Above equilibrium there is excess supply. Sellers competing to clear stock reduce the price, which draws in more buyers along the demand curve while making production less attractive along the supply curve, until the two quantities meet.

distractorRationale.b: Buyers bid price up only when there is excess demand, which happens below equilibrium
distractorRationale.c: Markets return to equilibrium without any government action; that is the point of the price mechanism
distractorRationale.d: The curves do not move; only the price and the quantities along them adjust
